reconcile.note: Henry distinguishes the barred fighting staff and street shoes in Matthew and Luke from the walking staff and sandals Mark permits.

discrepancy.note: Strauss identifies the packing-list itself as a discrepancy, traced to tradition preserving the staff-and-shoes detail two different ways.

quotes.text: Here, however, we find a discrepancy; according to Matthew and Luke, Jesus forbids the disciples to take with them, not only gold, a scrip, and the like, but even shoes , ὑποδήματα , and a staff , ῥάβδον ; according to Mark, on the contrary, he merely forbids their taking more than a staff and sandals , εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον and σανδάλια .
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, §77 (1846), on Matthew 10:10 and Mark 6:8.

sides.snippet: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
sides.verseText: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.

sides.snippet: He charged them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
sides.verseText: He charged them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
